name: Bloom Energy
day_summary: SATURDAY WEEKEND REVIEW — US MARKETS CLOSED; $252.02 LAST CLOSE (JUNE 26, −18.49%); PARABOLIC MOMENTUM NAME TAKES THE COMPLEX'S HARDEST HIT. No US equity trading June 27 (Saturday). BE last traded at $252.02 (June 26, −$57.16, −18.49% from $309.18) — by far the worst session in the AI/power/memory complex (vs. SK Hynix −8.36%, Micron −6.69%, NBIS −6.36%, NVDA −2.20%). This is the math of owning a stock up ~280% YTD: when the regime turns risk-off (SPX 7,354 below the 7,460 floor; VIX ~18.41 above the 17 gate) and the AI-capex trade de-risks, the most-crowded, highest-momentum vehicle gives back the most, fastest. No deal broke — the Oracle 2.8GW master agreement / Project Jupiter, the $5B Brookfield partnership, and the ~$20–24B backlog are intact — but an −18% single-session unwind into NFP week is the volatility you signed up for in a parabolic name. Day winner: BEARS, decisively — momentum unwound and de-risking ahead of the July 3 holiday gap compounded it.
long_pnl: longs are still sitting on a huge year (~+280% YTD even after this) but just gave back −18.49% in a single session; the give-back is a stark reminder that BE is a high-beta momentum vehicle, not a low-vol utility — the Oracle/Brookfield/power-for-AI thesis that drove the run is intact, but anyone who added near $300+ is now underwater on that tranche; the discipline here is to respect the volatility and not average down into a falling knife before the tape stabilizes
short_pnl: bears had the single best session in the complex: −18.49% rewarded the 'parabolic + crowded + priced-for-perfection' short into a risk-off tape; the structural danger for shorts is the same volatility cutting the other way — a power-for-AI name with a real $20–24B backlog can rip +15–20% on any risk-on reversal or fresh Oracle/Brookfield milestone, so a −18% day is a tactical win to manage, not a thesis to overstay

decision.horizon: 2–4 quarters · into the next print and Oracle/Project Jupiter milestones
decision.rationale: HOLD at LOW conviction — respect the volatility, do not add into the knife. The fundamental story is the best it's been: Bloom is the bellwether of the power-for-AI trade, with the Oracle 2.8GW master agreement (Project Jupiter), the $5B Brookfield partnership, and a ~$20–24B backlog underwriting years of fuel-cell demand for AI data centers — it's Aschenbrenner's largest disclosed long for a reason. But the stock is a parabolic, crowded momentum vehicle, and June 26's −18.49% is the proof: a name up ~280% YTD can shed nearly a fifth of its value in one risk-off session with no deal breaking. That makes position sizing and trim discipline the entire game. Holders with large gains should let winners run but trim into euphoria, not chase; new money does not buy an −18% candle into NFP week — wait for the tape to base and for the next print or an Oracle/Jupiter milestone to re-anchor. Cross-reference /situational-awareness: the thesis is structural; the stock is volatile.

The Oracle 2.8GW master agreement, the $5B Brookfield financing, and a ~$20–24B backlog give Bloom multi-year demand visibility, and the power-for-AI trade is one of the most durable secular themes in the book. Own it as a high-conviction theme expressed through a high-volatility instrument — sized so that an −18% day is survivable, which June 26 just demonstrated it must be.

analysis: Bloom Energy's −18.49% on June 26 was the headline move of the complex, and it is best understood not as news but as math: a stock up ~280% YTD is a parabolic, crowded momentum vehicle, and when the regime turns risk-off and the AI-capex trade de-risks, the most-crowded name gives back the most, fastest — with no deal breaking. The fundamental story is, if anything, the strongest in the power-for-AI group: the Oracle 2.8GW master agreement (Project Jupiter), the $5B Brookfield partnership, and a ~$20–24B backlog give Bloom multi-year demand visibility, and it's Aschenbrenner's largest disclosed long. That is exactly why the discipline matters. This is a sizing and timing question, not a thesis question: holders should let the core run but trim into euphoria rather than weakness, and new money does not buy an −18% candle into NFP week. Own the theme through this instrument only at a size where a −18% day is survivable — June 26 just proved it must be. Cross-reference /situational-awareness for the structural case.
